html:
SMTO-GWT-0037 — This computer's connection is managed from that computer

GUID: d602f2b7-430f-41fb-9ffd-1f48fe1c0ec6
Slug: gateway-identity-peer-owned
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • This computer connects to SMTO on its own (an Outbound Gateway). Its connection settings and security identity are controlled on that computer, so SMTO refused to change them from here. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and find the computer. If it is marked Outbound, its connection is controlled from that computer. Outbound Gateways connect to SMTO themselves, so SMTO can't edit, switch off, delete or reset their identity.
  2. Ask the person who installed the Gateway on that computer to change its settings there and restart the Gateway so it reconnects. When it reconnects, SMTO picks up the new name, address or identity from the Gateway itself.
  3. Once it shows Connected again, check the results of any Task that was running on it before you send new work there. A dropped or changed connection doesn't prove that earlier work on that computer didn't run.

What success looks like

  • The computer reconnects, shows Connected in the Gateways list with the expected name, and new Tasks run on it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed that computer's Gateway. Don't add the same computer again as a second Gateway to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway management refused the change because the record belongs to an outbound Gateway, whose connection, lifecycle and TLS identity are owned by the outbound peer (edits, disable/delete and server-side identity forgetting are rejected with 409).

What this means

  • Management rejected edits to a record whose lifecycle belongs to an outbound peer, or refused controller-side forgetting of an outbound TLS identity. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Management rejected edits to a record whose lifecycle belongs to an outbound peer, or refused controller-side forgetting of an outbound TLS identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect record transport and source, then locate the configured peer that owns connection setup.

How to fix it

  • Change outbound connection settings (for example SMTO_CONTROLLER_URL, node identity, enablement) in the Gateway's own configuration on its host and restart that Gateway so its hello re-registers the record. To replace its TLS identity, re-pair or reconnect from the peer and verify the new identity; the Server will not forget an outbound identity (gateway_management.check_gateway_mutation, forget_gateway_identity).
  • Manage outbound connection and lifecycle changes through the configured peer and verify its identity when reconnecting.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning peer's supported configuration establishes the intended connection and identity.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
